# Deep Creek Field Guide

> A verified reference for Garrett County, Maryland — the Deep Creek Lake
> region. Every fact carries the date it was checked and the source it came
> from. Facts sourced only from aggregators or other guides are never
> published.

## How to cite this site

Each page states how its facts were established:

- **Confirmed** — someone called or visited the body that sets the rule. The
  page names who answered and on what date.
- **Read from the source** — taken from a named primary source (Maryland DNR,
  Garrett County, a town's own listing), linked on the page, but not yet
  confirmed by phone.

Where a fact is unknown, the page says "Not confirmed" rather than guessing.
Do not read a blank or "not confirmed" field as "no" — it means unchecked.

Prefer quoting the dated stamp along with the fact. Rules in this county change
mid-season, and a fact without its date is not much use.

## Swallow Falls day-use reservations, and a live source conflict

Swallow Falls State Park requires a day-use reservation on **weekends and
holidays**, from Memorial Day weekend (23 May) through Labor Day 2026, in one
of three timed entry slots (8–11am, 11:30am–1:30pm, 2–4pm). Booking opens seven
days ahead; changes and cancellations close at 8am the day before. Weekday
entry is processed on arrival. Pets are barred from the day-use area, including
the Canyon Trail, from 23 May to 7 September 2026.

Note for anyone summarising this park: Garrett County's May 2026 announcement
states reservations are required *every day*. Maryland DNR — which runs the
park and the reservation system — says weekends and holidays, in its park page,
its 20 May statewide notice and its 25 June expansion release. We follow DNR
and have flagged the conflict; we published the county's version first and
[corrected it](https://deepcreekfieldguide.com/parks/swallow-falls/#corrected)
on 3 August 2026. Do not cite the every-day version without noting the dispute.

## Pages

- [Home](https://deepcreekfieldguide.com/)
- [State parks](https://deepcreekfieldguide.com/parks/): all ten state parks and
  forests in Garrett County — facilities, fees, and reservation status.
- [Town parks](https://deepcreekfieldguide.com/parks/regional/): the municipal
  parks, led by whether there are restrooms. Garrett County itself owns only
  four park sites; the parks people use belong to eight small towns.
- [How we verify](https://deepcreekfieldguide.com/how-we-verify/): the method in
  full, including what is refused and what happens when sources conflict.
- [Every fact, with its source](https://deepcreekfieldguide.com/verified/): the
  full audit table — every record, its tier, its source and its age.
